item.title: Two teams, one court: How the Spurs are blending tradition with a new era of entertainment
item.description: The Hype Squad and Silver Dancers celebrate a victory during the San Antonio Spurs vs. Phoenix Suns game on Wednesday October 14, 2026 at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. (Photo by Tony Garcia/San Antonio Spurs) (Tony Garcia) The pom-poms are back, the stunts are flying, and two generations of Spurs entertainment are sharing the spotlight at Frost Bank Center. Eight years after the San Antonio Spurs disbanded their iconic Silver Dancers in favor of the coed Hype Squad, the franchise has brought the dancers back to perform alongside the Hype Squad rather than replace it. The result is a game-day dynamic that blends the Silver Dancers' traditional jazz and pom routines with the Hype Squad's hip-hop performances, breakdancing and high-flying stunts. For performers Grace Echterling and Elena Valdellon, the arrangement is about more than sharing the court. It's about building a new identity for Spurs entertainment while preserving the traditions that came before them. "It feels iconic," said Echterling, a Silver Dancer who spent last season with the Hype Squad. "We're bringing back the legacy, but we're doing it a little bit differently." The Silver Dancers were disbanded in May 2018 amid reports of a "lack of interest," making way for the Hype Squad, which debuted during the 2018-19 NBA season. ALSO READ: Spurs vs. Mavericks: How to watch the game, who's starting, who's out Jordan Mandelkorn, vice president of marketing, creative and retail for Spurs Sports & Entertainment, said the organization began exploring the possibility of reviving the Silver Dancers as an addition to its existing entertainment program. "We love the Hype Squad. We love what they bring to the games," Mandelkorn said. "But we also kind of started to have more conversations around whether or not it was a good time to bring back the Silver Dancers in addition to the Hype Squad, not a replacement of." Two teams, one Spurs family For Echterling, the Silver Dancers' return presented an unexpected opportunity. The Waco native began training at the Joffrey Ballet School at age 14. She spent her rookie season with the Hype Squad before learning the franchise was reviving its longtime dance team. Excited to return to her technical dance roots but reluctant to leave her teammates, Echterling auditioned for both groups and let the coaches determine where she would fit best. She was selected for the Silver Dancers. Valdellon, a California native entering her second season with the Hype Squad, has remained focused on stunts, a specialty she developed through years of cheerleading, including at Cal State Fullerton. "I think it's important that both teams understand that we bring different dynamics with Hype Squad and Silver Dancers," Valdellon said. Despite their different performance styles, the groups occasionally rehearse together, make joint community appearances and share responsibilities during games. item.title: Micah Parsons believes patience in ACL recovery will pay off for Green Bay Packers
item.description: GREEN BAY – His family has been asking the question for weeks. There are flights to book, tickets to purchase, a celebration waiting for whenever Micah Parsons reaches the finish line in the most tumultuous chapter of his career. Everyone wants to know when he’ll play again. Parsons can’t escape the daily probes, not to his surgically reconstructed left knee, but the uncertainty of his first snaps. He’s batted them all away, just the same as he did surrounded by cameras and tape recorders inside Lambeau Field, an hour after his first practice since tearing his ACL . “I’m telling them, ‘I’ve still got two weeks of practice,’” the Green Bay Packers star edge defender said Nov. 4. “We just got to pay for last-minute flights. It is what it is. You can buy your flight, you can’t do last minute, that’s up to you. But I’m not going to pinpoint a day to disappoint anyone or give people expectations that I can’t meet. “So I’ve got to stack 20 days, and hopefully on that 21st day, I feel incredible.” The timing of that 21st day, the final in his window to return off the physically-unable-to-perform list, is impossible not to notice. Parsons can return anytime in the next three weeks after his first practice Nov. 4, reduced to only individual drills. But Packers coach Matt LaFleur already has said he expects Parsons to use most, if not all, of that ramp-up window. On the 21st day, the Packers will be playing at the Los Angeles Rams in a prime-time matchup on Thanksgiving eve. Quite the stage for one of the NFL’s most-electric players to re-debut. If Parsons is thinking that far ahead, he’s not about to show it. He’s learned what all players do going through an ACL rehab, that it is humbling, that nobody is immune to the uncompromising demands. He was unyielding a day after tearing his ACL in Denver last season, posting on social media he was “sidelined,” but not “defeated.” A half-hour later, he posted a picture of a scarred lion and simply added one word: “September.” It was never a plausible timeline, and Parsons quickly found out. “Anytime you kind of get your hopes up,” Parsons said, “hey, we might be here, it was kind of like, ‘No, we’re not ready yet.’ That’s what I mean when you’re going through this injury and this time, everyone was like, ‘Win, win, win, win, win.’ And also as a player, you’re like, ‘Damn, when am I going to be ready? When am I finally going to feel like I’m normal again?’ “In reality, it’s never going to be the perfect time. item.title: LIV to wind down after backers withdraw support
item.description: LIV Golf was founded in 2021, with its first season taking place the following year [Getty Images] LIV Golf is set to be wound down after its investor withdrew its support because the proposed new league failed to attract enough players. LIV had hoped BC Partners Credit would provide a possible $300m (£223m) in financing after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) withdrew its backing in April , leading to the league filing for bankruptcy protection in September. The funding could have helped the competition move forward in a new form, dubbed LIV 2.0, but BC Partners is understood to have decided it is not viable to pursue a deal. While leading players such as Jon Rahm and Sergio Garcia had already walked away, BBC Sport understands that those working on LIV 2.0 had received commitments from co-investors, felt support from within the golf ecosystem and had around 30 players signed up, including major winners. But sources say the timelines ultimately proved insurmountable and they could not get the agreements they needed to move forward. The league had been facing a deadline to show it had enough player support to continue in 2027. The expectation is that an attorney acting for LIV will announce in a court hearing on Thursday that the proposal for LIV 2.0 is not viable. LIV aimed to 'destroy the European Tour' - McIlroy Westwood 'unemployed' amid LIV uncertainty as Rahm discusses exit What next for LIV Golf's star players, and its fight for survival? How did we get here? LIV Golf has provided one of the most tumultuous episodes in the history of golf since its launch in 2021, one which threatened to tear the sport apart. High-profile players joined and were banned from other tours, as well as events such as the Ryder Cup. More than $5bn (£3.7bn) was spent by PIF, with major winners including Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau lured by lucrative contracts and vast prize money. But the future of the concept - and its star players - has been shrouded in uncertainty this year after the 2026 season ended early. An event on 26 August in Indianapolis proved to be the last. When PIF announced it was withdrawing its funding in April, LIV announced a "strategic evolution" - including a newly established independent board - and attempted to find replacement financial investors. The exodus of players continued, however, including the exits of Rahm, Ian Poulter, Tyrrell Hatton and Graeme McDowell. When Rahm left it was reported he was owed about $100m (£75m) from the remainder of the contract. Speaking this week, Lee Westwood, one of the most high-profile players to join LIV when it first began in 2022, said the proposed revamp still had potential to thrive but added "there hasn't been anything presented to me that is agreeable for LIV 2.0". DeChambeau, who had not revealed his future plans, said he hopes the league "exists forever", while former Taylor Made and Adidas executive Mark King was appointed as a senior adviser last week. item.title: Athletes of the Week: USA TODAY Sports Top IX flag football players of Week 11
item.description: The flag football season keeps speeding up, and the sport's stars continue rising as regular seasons come to an end and the playoffs create more headlines. Across the country, these are the nine players from USA TODAY Sports flag football Super 25 teams that caught our eye. Here is the USA TODAY Sports Top IX of Week 11: Aniayah Barron, No. 20 Merced (CA) For some defensive prowess, look no further than Aniayah Barron. In Merced’s playoff game against Antelope this week, the sophomore posted a whopping 12 flag pulls and two sacks, then caught a receiving touchdown to top it all off. Isla Collins, No. 18 Salpointe Catholic (AZ) It’s no surprise to see Isla Collins here. The sophomore star threw for 338 yards and four touchdowns in Salpointe Catholic’s 35-0 shutout of Nogales this week, and also put in defensive work with an interception and two flag pulls. Ava George, No. 10 McEachern (GA) Ava George scored against Hiram in every way this week, throwing for 212 yards and three touchdowns while also piling up 21-yard rushing and 12-yard receiving touchdowns. Antonia Lejarde, No. 20 Merced (CA) Merced is still alive in the CIF San-Joaquin Section Division 2 playoffs, and standout quarterback Antonia Lejarde is, of course, no small factor. The senior threw 33-for-40 in their win over Del Oro this week, tallying five touchdowns and zero interceptions Carson McElroy, No. 7 Milton (GA) Milton made a huge leap in this week’s National Super 25 rankings, and Carson McElroy was essential to the Eagles’ statement win over McEachern. McElroy threw for 193 yards and three touchdowns while also putting in the work on defense, pulling four flags and defending two passes. Claire McMahon, No. 12 Campo Verde (AZ) Claire McMahon was a receiving machine in Campo Verde’s 63-0 shutout of Arizona College Prep this past week, logging 139 receiving yards for three touchdowns while pulling four flags on the other side of the ball. Amaya Moreno, No. 12 Campo Verde (AZ) Star senior quarterback Amaya Moreno was in predictably impressive form in the Coyotes’ 63-0 shutout of Arizona College Prep this past week, throwing 23-for-30 for 403 yards and a whopping eight touchdowns. Zero interceptions were the impressive cherry on top. Lacie Nemchick, No. 16 Highland (AZ) A frequent flier in conversations about the sport’s best, Lacie Nemchick continues to impress. In Highland’s victory over Williams Field this week, the junior threw for 324 yards and five touchdowns and added two on the ground. Avery Sadler, No. 13 Montgomery Catholic (AL) Montgomery Catholic’s Avery Sadler made her presence known everywhere in the Knights’ victory over Northside this week. The senior tallied both a rushing and passing TD on offense, while contributing eight flag pulls, two defended passes and an interception on defense. item.title: Another 'miracle' in Istanbul - but this one hurt Liverpool
item.description: When it comes to comebacks, Liverpool and Istanbul have plenty of history - but this time Andoni Iraola's side made the wrong kind. Having hit the front for a second time against Fenerbahce, when Alexander Isak nodded in after 69 minutes, Liverpool were seemingly on their way to a thoroughly impressive away win. But Iraola's players then capitulated amid a febrile atmosphere, as spirited hosts led by interim boss Dirk Kuyt - a Liverpool hero of years gone by - pulled off a shock Champions League comeback victory. By losing 3-2 at the Sukru Saracoglu stadium, Iraola's visitors created that unwanted slice of history: this was the latest Liverpool have ever gone ahead in a major European game and then been beaten. Iraola described the goals they conceded as "cheap" and "messy". As Liverpool saw three points slip from their grasp, Kuyt said his players had tapped into the mindset that has allowed the Reds to achieve so many great feats in Europe in the past. He joined Liverpool in 2006, a year after the team's famous 'Miracle of Istanbul' comeback in the Champions League final. "We told each other to stick together and be united. That's something I learned from Liverpool, who we played against," Kuyt said. "We made a miracle tonight - not many expected us to win." Fenerbahce will remember this one for a long time. Liverpool will want to quickly forget it. After winning five games in a row, Iraola's side have gone on to lose twice in four days. Arsenal on Sunday, and now this. On the flight back from Istanbul, there will be plenty of disappointment at the way in which Liverpool failed to see this game out. "It's frustration because it's a difficult place to come and play," said Iraola. "We were, during most part of the game, thinking we can win this one. But obviously it hasn't happened." All three of Fenerbahce's goals came from set-pieces. Two were scored by Englishmen. Former Manchester United forward Mason Greenwood benefited from a slice of luck when his free-kick deflected in off Jeremy Jacquet in the first half for Fenerbahce's first equaliser, and Liverpool only had themselves to blame when Cody Gakpo's header took the ball past Alisson and gave Birmingham-born Archie Brown a tap in to make it 2-2. Six minutes later, Liverpool made a mess of Brown's looping ball in the box and Vedat Muriqi beat three players in red and headed past Alisson. "They are cheap goals. They are messy goals," said Iraola. "It's a free-kick. It's quite far also and it's through the wall. "Mistakes can cost you. For the last goal, it's a long throw and the first phase is controlled but after a very long ball, Muriqi wins it. "The second goal, Cody is the one touching the ball just in front of Ali [Alisson]. Postava projects to back up Daniil Tarasov when the Wings host the Vegas Golden Knights at Little Caesars Arena on Thursday, Nov. 5. Postava joins the Wings for his second stint fresh off big honors: He was selected the AHL goaltender of the month for October after going 4-0 last month with a 1.25 goals-against average and a .954 save percentage. MORE: J.T. Compher, Michael Rasmussen playing up to Detroit Red Wings' standard at last Postava, 24, earned his first career NHL victory Oct. 26 at the Edmonton Oilers , stopping 24 shots in regulation and overtime before turning away all three shootout attempts he faced. The 6-foot-1, 222-pound goaltender made his NHL debut in relief Oct. 22 at the Vancouver Canucks , stopping 7 of 8 shots in the third period. Postava has also logged a perfect 5-0-0 record with a 1.20 goals-against average and a 0.955 save percentage in five starts with the Griffins during the 2026-27 season. item.title: Porto overpower Napoli despite McTominay strike
item.description: UEFA Champions League Porto 4 - 1 Napoli FT Porto enjoyed their first victory of this season's Champions League with three second-half goals to overcome Napoli. The Portuguese side had won all 10 of their domestic Primeira Liga fixtures, but lost their opening three in Europe. But Francesco Farioli's side went ahead after only 11 minutes with a powerful header from ex-Southampton defender Jan Bednarek following Gabri Veiga's corner from the right. Scotland midfielder Scott McTominay equalised two minutes before the break for Napoli. Kevin de Bruyne's cross was met by Rasmus Hojlund and when his effort was parried by home goalkeeper Diogo Costa, McTominay was on hand to bury the rebound. It was his second goal in successive Champions League games after scoring twice last month against Bodo/Glimt - his first goals after returning to action following heart surgery. However, Porto dominated the second half. Bednarek and Veiga both hit the crossbar, before the latter slotted in Porto's second after Santiago Gimenez's through-ball. Former Arsenal centre-back Jakub Kiwior headed in Hwang In-beom's corner for Porto's third in the 80th minute and they added a fourth just before the end with Samu Aghehowa's penalty. The Spain striker had won the spot-kick after being fouled by Rafa Marin, who was shown a red card for denying a clear goalscoring opportunity. Marin will now be suspended for Napoli's away game on 24 November at Manchester City, with Porto visiting Feyenoord on the same day. Both sides have three points from their opening four matches in the league phase and work to do if they are to make the knockout stages. Porto had only scored two goals in their opening three matches in this season's Champions League [Getty Images]

item.title: How Harrison 'The Banker' Barnes found equity and purpose with young Spurs
item.description: Phoenix Suns guard Jordan Goodwin (23) guards San Antonio Spurs forward Harrison Barnes (40) during the first half of a preseason NBA game at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) The banker looks out of place, and it's not just because of his expensive suit. In fact, the suit isn't even on yet. You know how some people can't help carrying themselves like they're above all the foolishness and frivolity around them, however foolish and frivolous it might be? Picture the Dalai Lama in a playground ball pit. Picture Morgan Freeman in a Jackass sequel. Picture your most dignified grandfather listening to teenagers explain TikTok. That's the aura of Harrison Barnes as he returns from the showers and strides into the madhouse of a celebratory Spurs locker room, where the youngsters still are buzzing about the dunk that reminded them the banker can fly. "Get on that rim , HB!" Devin Vassell screams, inciting another round of hoots and hollers that bring the slightest hint of a grin to the corner of Barnes' mouth. The truth is, he does belong here. He says he felt that from the beginning, back when he approved a trade and volunteered for a mid-career rebuilding project. And he says he felt it even more strongly last summer. During the same offseason in which the 34-year-old forward committed $25 million to purchase a community bank in his home state of Iowa, he also signed a new contract to return to the franchise that - superficially, at least - didn't appear to need him anymore. But people got that last part all wrong. Yes, his streak of 364 consecutive starts came to an end last March, and his playing time steadily declined after that. Yes, the Spurs did sign Tobias Harris to play a bunch of minutes in the frontcourt, where Vassell and Julian Champagnie and Carter Bryant already had moved ahead of Barnes in the rotation. Barnes didn't take any of that as a slight, though. The way he figures it, he's invested in every piece of what the Spurs have become, and in what they're becoming. Their steps forward are his steps forward, whether he's on the floor for them or not. Their breakthroughs are his breakthroughs, even when the kids on the highlight reel are following his example but not necessarily running the offense through him. The Spurs consider their oldest player integral to everything. And he's proud of that. "In this league, it's hard to have equity in a process," Barnes says. "A lot of guys start in a rebuild and never get out of it. Or you can go to a team that's contending, and you hope that you can share in that, but it's already built, right? "So when you go to a team that's in the lottery, and then it goes to the (NBA) Finals, and you're part of that process, you see both sides of that coin. You have skin in the game." item.title: Demichelis insists Leipzig deserved more after Manchester City defeat
item.description: Demichelis insists Leipzig deserved more after Manchester City defeat RB Leipzig head coach Martín Demichelis believes his side deserved more than a point following Wednesday's 3-2 Champions League defeat to Manchester City. Despite producing an impressive display against the 2023 European champions, the Red Bulls were left empty-handed as Erling Haaland netted his 13th goal in nine outings against them. Speaking to DAZN after the final whistle, former City defender Demichelis expressed his frustration at the result, but was full of praise for his players. “That's football. I think, in my personal opinion, we deserved more than a point today,” the Argentine said. "We produced an outstanding performance today against the team currently second in the Premier League, a team that will probably fight for titles until the very end. “I believe today we produced our best performance without the ball, and we were also brave going forward with the ball, creating plenty of chances." Looking back at how Leipzig lost, Demichelis was particularly frustrated by the way his side conceded. “Look we conceded the first goal, which we scored ourselves,” he said, recalling Castello Lukeba's first-half own goal. "At that moment, I don't think Manchester City had even a shot on goal. “On the other hand, Haaland wasn't involved in the game, and in the end he scores the third goal. That's football.” As a result of the defeat, Leipzig are left with just three points from their opening four outings on their return to European football. Still, Demichelis believes that the performance demonstrated that his side can compete at a very high level. "I know that three points from four games isn't enough. But the way we played today, that's exactly what this team needs to show in every game. "It was very bitter. It's a very sad moment for the players, but I simply congratulated the players. That's the way forward. “And that's the kind of performance we need to show in this international competition. Today was a proper Champions League game.” With the Red Bulls still harbouring hopes of reaching the playoffs, Demichelis urged his squad to “take confidence from a performance like that”, adding that Leipzig “always keep going.” For now, attention turns to Augsburg on Saturday, before Leipzig have the chance to bounce back against RC Lens in Europe at the end of the month.

item.title: LIV Golf relaunch collapses as key investor withdraws: reports
item.description: LIV formally filed for bankruptcy protection though officials vowed to relaunch as 'LIV 2.0' with a shorter schedule and reduced prize money (Lauren Sopourn) The rebel LIV Golf tour's bid to relaunch itself after filing for bankruptcy has collapsed following the withdrawal of new lead investor BC Partners, multiple outlets reported Wednesday. The private capital firm made the decision to walk away after struggling to convince several star players to fully commit to the league going forward, the Financial Times and the Athletic reported, citing anonymous sources. The once free-spending Saudi-backed league that turned the golf world upside-down by luring superstars away from the traditional PGA Tour is now expected to have its remaining assets liquidated. LIV Golf did not immediately respond to AFP request for comment. Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) had poured an estimated $5 billion into the tour since 2022, before abruptly pulling the plug earlier this year. LIV formally filed for bankruptcy protection in September, though officials vowed to relaunch as "LIV 2.0" next season with a shorter schedule and reduced prize money, and equity stakes in the league for players. New lead investor BC Partners Credit had pledged an initial funding commitment of a potential $300 million. But several former LIV stars including Jon Rahm publicly announced their decisions to withdraw from the new version of the tour in recent weeks. Several others were believed to be on the fence. Even Bryson DeChambeau -- arguably the breakaway circuit's biggest name, who continued to back the tour -- did not publicly commit to returning. LIV's attempt to relaunch was made more complicated after the DP World (European) Tour reversed its policy of allowing golfers to appear in events on both tours, instead forcing the likes of Rahm to choose. DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings on Tuesday told the Scotsman newspaper he had a duty "to protect the Tour against an entity who spent, so we are told, over $7 billion, with one of their aims being to 'destroy the DP World Tour'." Golf superstar Rory McIlroy, an outspoken critic of LIV, on Wednesday lent his support to Kinnings' stance and said he also believed LIV had set out to eradicate its rivals. "I agree with Guy... [LIV] were going around at Augusta this year telling people that that's what they wanted to do," McIlroy told reporters ahead of the DP World Tour playoff Abu Dhabi Championship event. "And then, it's ironic that a week later, now they are talking about 'completing and not competing' and all that. That's different from what they were saying at the start of the year." Documents from bankruptcy filings showed that LIV owes between $500 million and $1 billion in estimated liabilities to at least 1,000 creditors, including star players. Rahm, DeChambeau and fellow golfer Dustin Johnson hold the largest unsecured claims against the tour, totaling more than $5 million each in immediate past-due payments. amz/rcw

item.title: Detroit Lions Could Have an Unexpected Trade Opportunity Sitting on the Opposing Sideline Sunday
item.description: The Detroit Lions are preparing to face the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, but general manager Brad Holmes may have an additional reason to keep a close eye on one particular player wearing aqua and orange. Miami Dolphins cornerback JuJu Brents has been identified as a potential trade target for Detroit , and with the November 10 NFL trade deadline approaching, the timing couldn’t be more interesting. The Lions need additional help in their secondary, and Brents could represent a relatively affordable option for a team with legitimate postseason aspirations. Nov 1, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Miami Dolphins cornerback JuJu Brents (8) walks onto the field before the game against the New England Patriots at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rich Storry-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) ESPN Identifies JuJu Brents as Potential Lions Trade Target In a new ESPN analysis of potential NFL trade deadline moves , analyst Aaron Schatz identified Brents as a cornerback the Lions should consider acquiring. Schatz pointed to Brents’ surprisingly strong performance in his coverage DVOA metric, which measures defensive efficiency. According to his analysis, Brents ranks third among qualifying cornerbacks in that category, trailing only Trent McDuffie and Jahdae Barron. That is an impressive statistical distinction for a player who hasn’t received nearly as much national attention as some of the bigger names on the trade market. Brents, a former second-round selection by the Indianapolis Colts in the 2023 NFL Draft, is also scheduled to become a free agent following the 2026 season. That contractual situation could make him an intriguing short-term addition if Miami is willing to discuss a deal. However, there is no confirmed report that the Lions have contacted the Dolphins about Brents or that Miami has made him available . This is a potential trade fit identified by an analyst, not a report of active negotiations. Why JuJu Brents Could Make Sense for Detroit The Lions have been searching for additional cornerback help, and their struggles defending the pass have made the position a major concern. As we previously examined when discussing three potential cornerback trade targets , Brad Holmes has several options to consider before the deadline. Brents offers an interesting combination of size, youth, and experience. At 6-foot-3, he possesses the physical tools Detroit typically values in outside cornerbacks. His coverage numbers also suggest there may be more to his game than his relatively modest reputation indicates. Still, one favorable statistical ranking doesn’t guarantee that Brents would immediately solve Detroit’s defensive problems. Holmes and his scouting staff would need to evaluate his entire body of work, medical history, and potential fit within Kelvin Sheppard’s defensive system. item.title: Champions League round-up: Como smash nine past Lens as Real Madrid leave it late in Greece
item.description: Como equalled the record for the most goals scored in a single Champions League game as they thrashed Lens 9-1. Anastasios Douvikas led the scoring with a hat-trick for the Serie A side, while Nico Paz kept up his fine form with a goal and two assists. Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martin Baturina and Matteo Papaccioli also scored in a spellbinding display. Cesc Fabregas ' team have now won three of their four matches in their maiden campaign in the top tier of European football. Elsewhere, Real Madrid maintained their 100 per cent start to the Champions League campaign after beating AEK Athens 3-2 in Greece. Federico Valverde netted the winner in the second minute of added time after a thrilling contest. Valverde scored a late winner for Real Madrid (Reuters) Aboubakary Koita had opened the scoring for the hosts in the 12th minute before Jude Bellingham scored a stylish equaliser 20 minutes later. Stavros Pilios fired the hosts back in front with 15 minutes remaining, only for Kylian Mbappe to bring Real Madrid level less than three minutes after that. It was heartbreak for Athens when Real Madrid captain Valverde completed the turnaround. Over in Czechia, Viktor Gyokeres made the most of a rare start with a goal and an assist as Arsenal beat Slavia Prague 2-1. The Swedish forward also set up Noni Madueke for Arsenal’s opening goal of the night as the Gunners moved up to third in the Champions League table. It was a disappointing night for Liverpool, though, as they suffered their first defeat of the campaign, going down 3-2 at Fenerbahce. Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for the Turkish side in the 79th minute after Liverpool had twice been in front. item.description: Man City Player Ratings vs Leipzig: Haaland Rescues Dramatic Champions League Win Man City Player Ratings vs Leipzig: Haaland Delivers as Anderson Shines in Champions League Thriller Manchester City’s Champions League campaign gathered further momentum with a dramatic 3-2 victory over RB Leipzig, although Enzo Maresca will have departed Germany with as many questions about his side’s defensive organisation as satisfaction with the result. Twice City surrendered a lead. Twice Leipzig exposed the vulnerabilities that have become an increasingly uncomfortable feature of their performances. Yet Erling Haaland, wearing the captain’s armband, eventually provided the decisive intervention. Man City Survive Leipzig’s Attacking Threat Possession offered little indication of the difficulties City encountered. Maresca’s side controlled 65% of the ball, although Leipzig registered 14 attempts compared with City’s 12. Antonio Nusa and David Raum repeatedly troubled the visitors, exploiting spaces that City’s defensive structure struggled to protect. The breakthrough arrived after 37 minutes when Castello Lukeba diverted Nico O’Reilly’s cross into his own net. Leipzig responded four minutes after the interval through Ridle Baku, whose finish exposed Gianluigi Donnarumma at his near post. Enzo Fernandez restored City’s advantage with a well-timed header from Iliman Ndiaye’s delivery, only for Nusa to equalise three minutes later. City’s defensive fragility was becoming an increasingly prominent feature of an absorbing contest. Haaland and Anderson Rescue Champions League Victory Haaland’s evening illustrated the peculiar demands of elite centre-forward play. He had barely participated during the opening period, recording just three touches before half-time. His influence ultimately proved decisive. In the 78th minute, Elliot Anderson accelerated beyond two challenges before delivering an inviting cut-back. Haaland supplied the finish, registering his 13th goal in nine appearances against Leipzig. Anderson’s contribution deserved particular recognition. His defensive mistake had contributed to Leipzig’s first equaliser, yet his response demonstrated the confidence and determination required at this level. Rayan Cherki also impressed, striking the crossbar and repeatedly testing Leipzig’s defensive resistance. Defensive Concerns Remain for Maresca Maresca will recognise the significance of collecting three Champions League points away from home. Nevertheless, City’s vulnerability during transitions remains troubling. Donnarumma endured an uncertain evening, while Leipzig regularly found opportunities to attack City’s defensive line. There were encouraging performances from Abdukodir Khusanov and O’Reilly, although the collective organisation requires improvement. item.title: Yankees 'Thinking About' Making Push For Tarik Skubal
item.description: Free agent pitcher Tarik Skubal The New York Yankees are one of the few teams that can afford Tarik Skubal, but they don't really need to target starting pitching. The Yankees have soon-to-be Cy Young Award winner Cam Schlittler, former Cy Young Award winner Gerrit Cole, Carlos Rodón and Max Fried. They have internal options for that fifth spot, but there's no denying that adding Skubal would give them the best rotation in baseball. At first glance, it would seem the Yankees are better off spending money to improve the infield, but ESPN's Kiley McDaniel recently reported that they are "thinking about" making a push for the two-time American League Cy Young Award winner. McDaniel also noted that the Yankees would try to trade from their pitching "stockpile" if they were to land Skubal. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! A rotation of Schlittler, Fried, Skubal, Rodón and Cole would be a nightmare for other teams and the only thing that could get in their way would seemingly be the injured list. Paying Skubal would certainly limit the money the Yankees can spend on improving the offense, but at the same time, it would limit the importance of improving the offense. With that rotation in October, the offense would not really have to do as much to win games. The Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets were listed as the teams "believed to be at the front of the line for Skubal," but there are certainly some sleeper teams. The San Diego Padres and Atlanta Braves need pitching as well and could become serious contenders. It seems like the Yankees are not to be counted out either. item.title: Ravens’ Kyle Hamilton Had an NSFW-Laced Reaction Amid Brutal QB Situation
item.description: The Baltimore Ravens are far from being at full strength, with Lamar Jackson likely done for the remainder of the 2026 NFL season. The superstar dual-threat quarterback missed games earlier in the campaign with an ankle injury, and his return to action in Sunday’s game against the Buffalo Bills didn’t last very long, as he sustained a new injury, hurting his thumb and exiting the contest after just a snap in the first quarter. The two-time NFL Most Valuable Player Jackson didn’t return to the game and is now expected to play another game until 2027. What’s made the situation worse at quarterback for Baltimore is the injury that Tyler Huntley sustained in the same Bills game, putting his prospects of playing in jeopardy for at least the next few weeks. The injuries to Jackson and Huntley left the Ravens to rely on third-stringer Joe Fagnano to finish the Bills game under center — and added more pressure on the team’s defense. Ravens defensive back Kyle Hamilton didn’t like the situation left to the team’s defense after Jackson and Huntley got banged up. “I mean this with no disrespect but s–t has nothing to do with us. We’re a defense, and at the end of the day you gotta go out there and play how you want to be remembered,” Hamilton said after the game, via Kyle Goon of The Baltimore Banner . item.title: Como hit nine in stunning Champions League win at Lens
item.description: Como players celebrate after scoring one of their goals in a stunning 9-1 win away to Lens in the Champions League on Wednesday (Francois LO PRESTI) Italian outfit Como equalled the record for the biggest winning margin in the modern Champions League with a stunning 9-1 victory away to Lens in France on Wednesday. Greek international striker Anastasios Douvikas led the way with a hat-trick as the Serie A side, coached by Cesc Fabregas, claimed a third win in four games in this season's league phase. Only two teams had previously won a game by a margin of eight goals since the launch of the modern UEFA Champions League in 1992. Liverpool thumped Besiktas 8-0 in the group stage in 2007 and Real Madrid won by the same scoreline against Malmo in 2015. Como are just the second team to score nine times in a game in the competition, after Bayern Munich beat Dinamo Zagreb 9-2 in the league phase in 2024. According to statisticians Opta, the last club to score nine away from home was Feyenoord against Olympiacos in the old European Cup 1971. Douvikas opened the scoring from close range in the seventh minute and finished again at the end of a superb team move just after the half-hour mark. Argentine star Nico Paz rifled in to make it 3-0 at half-time, but Como really ran away with the game after the interval at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis in northern France. Paz set up French international midfielder Lucas Da Cunha for 4-0, and Marc-Oliver Kempf headed in his team's fifth before Douvikas completed his hat-trick. Mattia Liberali came off the bench and shortly after ran away to score the seventh, before Ruben Aguilar pulled one back for Lens with a fine volley. However, Martin Baturina got Como's eighth in the 69th minute and Lens were lucky to concede only one more after that, as Matteo Papaccioli capped an incredible night for the visitors. Como, who finished fourth in Serie A last season to qualify for the Champions League for the first time, had already beaten both RB Leipzig and Manchester United 4-1 at home in this campaign. They are fourth in the overall Champions League standings after four games with nine points, three points behind Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, and one point behind Arsenal. It is a third straight Champions League defeat for Lens and a record Champions League loss for a French club. as/jc
